label.en: Statutory monthly gross minimum wage, 30th of June

description.en: $MinWage is the French statutory gross monthly minimum wage (SMIC), captured as of 30 June each year (currently €1,867.02) and defined once in SetDefault_fr as a system-wide wage benchmark for the FR spine. It is referenced in ConstDef_fr/DefConst when building $mc_yem_max, part of the parameter set for the COVID-19 wage-compensation schemes, and is used as the Comp_Cond eligibility condition in tscse_fr/BenCalc's self-employed 'Family benefits-SIC' contribution calculation. More broadly, French social-contribution rules frequently set contribution-rate cut-offs and relief thresholds as multiples of the minimum wage — the FR contributions documentation expresses several employer contribution-rate changes and the low-wage 'Réduction générale'/RGDU relief in terms of SMIC multiples — which is the general role $MinWage plays as a reference value elsewhere in the model.

description.en: $Minwage_hourly is the gross hourly minimum wage (SMIC horaire brut). It is defined once in SetDefault_fr and reused across the spine as a threshold for dependent-child and eligibility tests: TUDef_fr/DefTu, bchlg_fr/DefTu and bhotn_fr/DefTu use it (via DepChildCond) to decide whether a child counts as a dependent — per bhotn.md and bch00.md, a child under 20 is dependent only if earning less than 55% of the minimum wage — while bch00_fr/BenCalc uses the same 55%-of-minimum-wage test to gate the fixed monthly amount paid to families with 3+ children when the eldest is 20 (bch00.md gives the resulting euro thresholds, e.g. 1104.25 EUR from April 2025). It is also used in bmact_fr/BenCalc and bpact_fr/BenCalc as part of a previous-insurance-record eligibility check, and in bsawk_fr/ArithOp to help compute the activity bonus (Prime d'Activite). The label '30th of June' appears to be an internal modeller note on the constant's update/reference date rather than a policy description.

label.en: PSS: Plafond Annuel de la Sécurité Sociale

description.en: $PSS ('Plafond Annuel de la Sécurité Sociale') is France's official annual social-security earnings ceiling, defined once in ConstDef_fr and used as a scaling constant at 33 sites across the FR spine — the single most widely referenced constant in this batch. Examples include tinty_fr/DefConst, which uses it to build the $csg_red_thres threshold for determining net taxable income (RNI) in the personal income tax module, and tscse_fr, which uses PSS multiples throughout the self-employed contribution schedule: as the SchedCalc lower limit for the artisan/industry-and-trade 'MAIN' pension-insurance band, as the BenCalc eligibility condition for artisan sickness-insurance contributions, and in the artisan professional-training-contribution formula. The Country Report (tscse.md, Table 2.63) documents PSS rising from €41,136 in 2022 to €47,100 in 2025; the model's latest value of €48,060 continues this annual uprating, and multiples of PSS (1×, 1.1×, 1.4×, 4×, 5×) define almost every self-employed contribution income band described in the report's Table 2.64.

label.en: Minimum age to receive a full state pension

description.en: $RetAge_full is the age at which an individual becomes entitled to a full-rate state pension in France (currently 67, a value that has changed only once since the constant's introduction in 2006). It is read inside bunct_fr's Elig function (elig_cond parameter), which sets the eligibility flag for the unemployment insurance benefit ARE, where it is used together with $RetAge_min to bound ARE eligibility by the claimant's age. This is consistent with the country report's note that ARE eligibility is age-tested at the end of the income reference period, so individuals past pension age are treated as ineligible for the benefit. The exact pension-age legislation behind the figure is not detailed in the read sources (the benefits theme note covers only ARE's contribution/amount rules), so this reading rests mainly on the constant's name, label and its Elig usage site.

label.en: Minimum age to receive a state pension

description.en: $RetAge_min is the minimum legal age from which a state pension can be drawn in France (latest value 62.75 years, recorded through four value changes since 2006, consistent with the successive French pension reforms that progressively raised the minimum retirement age). Like $RetAge_full, it is used only in bunct_fr's Elig elig_cond, forming part of the age-based eligibility test for the unemployment insurance benefit (ARE), so the model restricts ARE receipt for people who have reached (or passed) minimum pension age. The country report confirms an age condition is applied when simulating ARE eligibility but does not spell out the exact thresholds used, so the precise interplay between $RetAge_min and $RetAge_full is inferred from their names, labels and shared usage site rather than stated explicitly in the sources.

label.en: Qualifying period: min no of months in work

description.en: $UB_QperMin is the minimum number of months a claimant must have worked within the qualifying reference window to be eligible for the unemployment insurance benefit ARE (Allocation de retour a l'emploi). It is used in bunct_fr's BenCalc (Comp_perElig, the component commented 'eligibility: no of months worked in qualifying period') and in bunct_fr's Elig (elig_cond) to test the claimant's work history against this minimum. Per the country report, since November 2019 claimants must have worked at least 6 months (the constant's current value) over the qualifying window, versus 4 months under the pre-November-2019 rules; the requirement was also temporarily cut to 4 months from August 2020 to November 2021 because of the Covid-19 crisis, which is reflected in the constant's three recorded value changes since 2006.

label.en: Qualifying period for 53 year old or older

description.en: $UB_age53plus_QperTot historically extended the ARE qualifying reference window (see $UB_QperTot) to 36 months for claimants aged 53 and over, mirroring the country report's rule that workers 53+ have a longer look-back period than the standard 24 months. It is used only within bunct_fr's BenCalc Comp_perElig qualifying-period-eligibility component. Its latest recorded value is 'n/a' (no longer set), which lines up with the benefits theme note's 2025-to-2026 change entry showing the extended-qualifying-period age threshold moving from '53+' to '55+' - i.e. this constant appears to have been superseded by $UB_age55plus_QperTot. The three historical value periods recorded since 2006 likely reflect the legislative history of the 53+ threshold prior to that replacement.

label.en: Qualifying period for 55 year old or older

description.en: $UB_age55plus_QperTot is the current extended ARE qualifying reference window (36 months) applicable to claimants aged 55 and over, used in bunct_fr's BenCalc Comp_perElig alongside the standard $UB_QperTot (24 months, for the under-55s). It replaces the former 53+ age threshold recorded in $UB_age53plus_QperTot: the benefits theme note explicitly shows the ARE eligibility rule changing from '36 months for 53+' in 2025 to '36 months for 55+' from 2026, with the identical shift appearing in the 'Contribution Requirement' row of the ARE summary table. This aligns the unemployment-benefit qualifying-period age threshold with the broader upward shift in French retirement/labour-market age thresholds noted elsewhere in the country's reforms.

label.en: Fixed daily amount- FYA (12.12+12.47)/2

description.en: $UB_dayfixamt is the flat daily allocation added to 40.4% of the daily reference wage (SJR) when computing the ARE unemployment benefit; it is used as one of the Val operands of bunct_fr's Max function that determines the monthly benefit amount. Per the country report, the benefit equals '40.4% of the SJR + the fixed allocation', with that fixed allocation rising from about 12.12-12.47 EUR/day in 2022 to 13.11 EUR/day in 2025 (Table 2.46), and the benefits theme note gives 13.18 EUR/day as the 2026 update, matching the constant's latest value. The label's '(12.12+12.47)/2' reflects the country report's note that, because the amount is uprated mid-year (each 1 July), the model represents the annual figure with a weighted 'FYA' (first-year average) combining the pre- and post-July amounts.

label.en: Minimum daily amount- Value as of 30th of june

description.en: $UB_dayminamt is the minimum (floor) daily ARE benefit amount, valued as of 30 June each year, i.e. before the annual 1 July uprating described in the country report. It is used as the LowLim parameter of both bunct_fr's ArithOp and bunct_fr's Max functions (the latter computing the final monthly benefit), ensuring the benefit paid never falls below this daily floor. The value matches the country report's 'Minimum Benefit'/'Floor' figures in Tables 2.46-2.47 (31.97 EUR/day at end-June 2025), and the benefits theme note's 2026 update of 32.13 EUR/day corresponds to the constant's latest recorded value.

description.en: $UB_rate1 is the 40.4% rate applied to the gross daily reference wage (SJR) as the first of two ways of computing the ARE daily benefit, per the country report: 'the amount of the benefit is 40.4% of the SJR + the fixed allocation' ($UB_dayfixamt). It is used as a Val operand of bunct_fr's Max function, which then takes the higher of this option and the $UB_rate2 (57% of SJR) option to determine the final benefit amount, a rule in force since 1 July 2014.

description.en: $UB_rate2 is the 57% rate applied to the gross daily reference wage (SJR), the second ('alternative') basis for the ARE daily benefit. Per the country report, since 1 July 2014 the benefit paid is the higher of (40.4% of SJR + fixed allocation, i.e. $UB_rate1 + $UB_dayfixamt) and (57% of SJR, this constant), which the report describes as making the benefit equal to between 57% and 75% of SJR. It is used as the second Val operand of bunct_fr's Max function alongside $UB_rate1.

description.en: $UB_red_thres is the monthly gross-wage threshold above which the ARE benefit is reduced by 30% from the 7th month of unemployment (the 'degressivity'/high-earner reduction introduced 1 December 2021). It is used in bunct_fr's BenCalc as the Comp_Cond condition of the component commented 'reduction for high salaries from 7th month (since December 2021)', i.e. that reduction component is only triggered once the claimant's gross wage exceeds this threshold. The country report and benefits theme note describe this threshold as annually indexed and age-restricted (applying only below an age cut-off, itself lowered from 57 to 55 from April 2025), rising from about 4518 EUR/month in 2020 to 4915.33 EUR/month in 2025; the constant's latest value of 4940 continues this upward indexation.

label.en: ASS daily benefit amount

description.en: Daily benefit amount for the Allocation de Solidarité Spécifique (ASS), the unemployment assistance benefit paid to jobseekers who have exhausted their unemployment insurance (ARE) rights, were employed at least 5 years in the last 10, are under the eligibility age, able to work, and actively seeking a job. It is defined in the general constants policy (ConstDef_fr) and used in bunmt_fr's BenCalc function (Comp_Cond parameter, commented 'Benefit amount') as the daily rate underlying the benefit: the monthly amount equals this daily figure times 30 when the couple's net taxable income is below the full-rate threshold (40x the daily amount for a single person, 80x for a couple), and is reduced pound-for-pound above that threshold up to the income ceiling (70x/110x the daily amount). The value 19.48 EUR/day corresponds to the 2026 rate, up from 19.33 EUR/day in 2025.

label.en: Maximum wage compensation

description.en: Upper bound on the "real" monthly Covid-19 wage-compensation benefit that yemcomp_fr (EUROMOD's model of France's chômage partiel/activité partielle scheme) pays, applied as UpLim in its "'real' monthly benefit paid by the state while in compensation scheme" BenCalc. In the model it is defined as the formula $MinWage * 4.5 (4.5 times the minimum wage/SMIC, scaled by hours worked), directly matching the France Country Report's description that state reimbursement is capped "up to 4.5 SMIC" (e.g. €6,927 in 2021, €7,152.75 in 2022). It carries no value ("n/a") in current systems because yemcomp_fr is switched off outside the 2020-2022 crisis years it was designed for.

In the model it is defined as the formula $MinWage (the minimum wage/SMIC itself, e.g. €1,539.42/month in 2020), scaled by hours worked and the relevant payer's share of the compensation. label.en: FYA: replacement rate applied to the salary (weighted average values for each month)

description.en: Represents the wage-replacement rate applied to an employee's salary under France's Covid-19 short-time-work ('activité partielle') wage-compensation scheme, modelled in the spine as policy yemcomp_fr (Country Report section 'Wage compensation scheme in response to Covid-19', bwkmcee_s). It feeds the Comp_perTU formula of yemcomp_fr's BenCalc function, whose comment describes the component as computing the 'real' monthly benefit paid while a worker is in the compensation scheme. The Country Report shows this rate changing several times over 2020-2022 (70% of the gross wage, i.e. 84% of net, from March 2020; falling to 60%/72% for most sectors from July 2021, while protected sectors such as tourism and hospitality kept 70%); consistent with the constant's own label, the value stored for each period is a weighted average of the different monthly rates that applied within that period rather than a single snapshot figure. The scheme, and hence this constant, only produces an effect when the model is run together with the LMA labour-market-transitions add-on, since it is switched off in the standard baseline.

label.en: FYA: share of the wage compensation paid by the state (weighted average of values for each month)

description.en: Represents the share of the wage compensation under the same Covid-19 short-time-work scheme (yemcomp_fr, Country Report section 'Wage compensation scheme in response to Covid-19', bwkmcee_s) that is funded by the French state, as opposed to the amount the employer itself still has to pay. It is combined with $mc_yem_rrate in the Comp_perTU formula of yemcomp_fr's BenCalc, whose comment identifies the component as computing the 'real' monthly amount paid by the firm, i.e. the compensation net of what the administration reimburses. The Country Report's tables document this state-funded share falling over time (around 70% of the gross wage in March-May 2020, roughly 60-63% for most sectors from mid-2020, dropping to 52% in June 2021 and 36% from July-November 2021 for non-protected sectors, before returning to 70% in December 2021-February 2022, with protected sectors such as tourism/hospitality kept at 70% throughout), the employer covering the remainder; as with $mc_yem_rrate, the constant stores a weighted average of these month-varying shares for each period. Like the rest of the scheme, it is only active when EUROMOD is run with the LMA add-on.

label.en: Average amount of the self-employment compensation scheme (from official statistics)

description.en: Represents the flat average lump-sum amount paid to a self-employed person under France's Covid-19 solidarity-fund compensation scheme ('fonds de solidarité'), modelled as policy ysecomp_fr (Country Report section 'Self-employed and firm compensation scheme in response to Covid-19', bwkmcse_s). It is used as the Comp_perTU value in ysecomp_fr's BenCalc function, whose comment describes it as a 'one-off benefit paid by the state when in compensation scheme', i.e. added as a single lump sum rather than simulated month by month. The Country Report explains that, because the EUROMOD dataset has no information on individual firms'/self-employed turnover losses, all eligible self-employed are instead assigned the actual average benefit recorded in official statistics: 1,278 EUR in 2020 and 2,272 EUR in 2021 and 2022, matching this constant's own label ('from official statistics'). As with the related Covid-19 policies, it only generates an effect when the model is run with the LMA labour-market-transitions add-on.

description.en: Constant intended to hold the duration, in months, of France's temporary Covid-19 self-employment compensation scheme modelled by ysecomp_fr ("self-employment compensation scheme Covid-19"), defined alongside the other pandemic-era wage/self-employment compensation constants in ConstDef_fr. In the model it was actually populated with real values only for 2020 (3 months) and 2021 (2 months) before reverting to "n/a"; however it is never referenced by any formula anywhere in the spine or add-ons (0 usage sites) — ysecomp_fr's BenCalc instead multiplies $mc_yse_amt (the average monthly compensation from official statistics) by the number of months actually spent in the scheme (variable bwkmcsemy_s, populated via the labour-market-transitions/LMA mechanism), so this constant has no effect on simulated results.

description.en: Represents the annual ceiling on overtime/extra-hours pay ('heures supplémentaires') that is exempt from personal income tax (and referenced alongside social insurance contributions, "SIC") in France; the latest value is €7,500 per year (raw "7500#y"), with three recorded historical values reflecting changes to the ceiling over time. It is defined in the shared constants policy ConstDef_fr but consumed in tinty_fr's ArithOp function (Formula parameter, "Non-exempted overtime pay (from 2019)"), where it is used to compute the portion of overtime earnings that becomes taxable once this exemption limit is exceeded. This aligns with France's 2019 exemption of overtime pay from income tax, later raised under the 2022 purchasing-power law; that reading is based on the constant's name, label and usage rather than the supplied theme/CR excerpts, which do not cover it explicitly.

It is used in tscee_fr/SchedCalc as the upper limit (Band_UpLim) of the band for the non-white-collar complementary pension contribution, and in tscer_fr/BenCalc (Comp_perTU) for the employer's basic old-age insurance contribution. Per tscee.md (Table 2.56), Income group 1 spans 0 to 1x monthly PSS, i.e. 3925 EUR/month in 2025 ('3925=1*monthly PSS'); the constant's latest value of 4005 reflects a further PSS revaluation.

In tscee_fr/SchedCalc it is the Band_UpLim of the non-white-collar complementary-pension band ('Complementary insurance for non white collar'), and it also bounds the AGFF contribution formula (Comp_perElig) in tscee_fr/BenCalc and the employer-side AGFF component (Comp_perTU, 'AGFF (old age)') in tscer_fr/BenCalc. description.en: $bma_max is the daily upper limit applied to the maternity/paternity/adoption leave benefit that replaces earnings while a parent is on statutory leave. In the model it caps the 'Daily amount per eligible parent' component of the maternity leave calculation (bmact_fr/BenCalc, parameter Comp_UpLim) and the paternity/adoption leave benefit (bpact_fr/ArithOp, parameter UpLim), so the same ceiling governs both schemes. Per the French Country Report, maternity/paternity daily allowances follow the same computation as sickness benefit (Indemnités Journalières de Sécurité Sociale) except for the maximum, which is instead calculated as 79% of the monthly social security ceiling (PSS) divided by 30.42 days — a different, higher cap than the plain sickness-benefit maximum (around €41-42/day per the sickness-benefits documentation). In the current extract this constant's recorded value is the non-numeric placeholder 'n/a' (unchanged since 2006-01-01), so no explicit euro figure is captured in this dataset.

Per the Country Report, maternity and paternity leave pay follow the same social-insurance rules as sickness benefit (Indemnités Journalières de Sécurité Sociale, a contributory earnings-related daily allowance subject to minimum/maximum ceilings), so this floor is a feature shared across that family of income-replacement benefits rather than being maternity/paternity-specific. label.en: Amount for children with one parent -FYA

description.en: $bchor_amt1 is the monthly rate of the Family Support Allowance (Allocation de soutien familial, ASF) paid per eligible dependent child living with a lone parent — cases where the other parent is deceased, has abandoned the child, or fails to pay maintenance — corresponding to the 'child living with lone parent' row of Country-Report Table 2.17. It is used in the defining bchor_fr policy's own BenCalc function as the Comp_perElig value, so it is added once for every eligible dependent child (generally under 20) who satisfies that lone-parent eligibility condition. ASF is not means-tested and not subject to income tax but is liable to CRDS; per the country report the benefit is currently simulated only for children of widows/widowers, since children abandoned by a parent or with unpaid alimony cannot be identified in the underlying survey data. The '-FYA' tag flags that the figure is a full-year weighted average combining the pre- and post-change amounts of in-year rate rises (e.g. the 4% increase on 1 July 2022 and the further single-parent-priority increase on 1 November 2022); the latest value of 201.79 EUR/month matches the 2026 lone-parent ASF rate given in the benefits theme document (up from 200.18 EUR in 2025).

It is used in the defining bchor_fr policy's own BenCalc function as the Comp_perElig value, added once per eligible dependent child meeting the corresponding no-parents eligibility condition. Like $bchor_amt1, ASF is not means-tested and not taxable but is subject to CRDS; the country report notes, however, that the model cannot identify children whose both parents are deceased, so in practice ASF is currently simulated only via the widow(er) scenario captured by $bchor_amt1, and this constant preserves the statutory 'no parents' rate for completeness of the legal parameter set. The '-FYA' tag indicates the value is a full-year weighted average of the amounts before/after 2022's in-year increases (4% on 1 July, plus the single-parent-priority rise on 1 November); the latest value, 268.97 EUR/month, matches the 2026 'no parents' ASF rate in the benefits theme document (up from 266.83 EUR in 2025).

description.en: $tscer_red_coef1 is the capped (maximum) value of the 'Reduction Fillon'/'Reduction generale des cotisations patronales' coefficient — the general reduction in employer social-security contributions on low wages — applicable to firms with fewer than 50 employees. It is used in tscer_fr/BenCalc as Comp_UpLim when 'calculating the applicable reduction coefficient', i.e. it caps the coefficient computed from the ratio of the annualised SMIC to the employee's gross annual income. Per tscer.md (Table 2.60), this cap was 0.3195 in 2022 and 0.3193 in 2025; the current value (0.3981) is markedly higher, plausibly reflecting the 'Reduction Generale Degressive Unique' (RGDU) reform noted in contributions.md, which extends the reduction to incomes up to 3 SMIC from 2026, though the sources do not spell out the exact 2026 formula.

description.en: $tscer_red_coef2 is the counterpart cap of $tscer_red_coef1 for firms with 50 or more employees, also used as Comp_UpLim in tscer_fr/BenCalc's applicable-reduction-coefficient calculation. Per tscer.md (Table 2.61), this cap was 0.3235 in 2022 and 0.3233 in 2025; the current value (0.4021) is substantially higher, likely reflecting the 2026 'Reduction Generale Degressive Unique' (RGDU) restructuring mentioned in contributions.md, although the exact new formula is not detailed in the available sources.

description.en: $tscer_red_coef3 is a component of the same 'Reduction Fillon'/RGDU employer-contribution-reduction coefficient calculation in tscer_fr/BenCalc, where it is used as Comp_LowLim. Its value (0.02) has changed only once since 2006, and is numerically exactly the gap between the Comp_UpLim caps ($tscer_red_coef1/$tscer_red_coef2) and the corresponding $tscer_red_coef5/$tscer_red_coef6 values, suggesting it functions as a lower-bound offset within the coefficient formula rather than as an independent contribution rate. Tscer.md's description of the reduction mechanism predates this apparent 2026 restructuring, so this component's precise role could not be independently confirmed from the available sources.

description.en: $tscer_red_coef5 is a '<50 employees' calibration value in the same employer-contribution-reduction coefficient calculation in tscer_fr/BenCalc, used as Comp_perTU. Its value (0.3781) equals $tscer_red_coef1 (the Comp_UpLim cap, 0.3981) minus $tscer_red_coef3 (the Comp_LowLim, 0.02), indicating it is a derived calibration point in the piecewise 'Reduction Fillon'/RGDU formula rather than a literal flat per-tax-unit amount. This apparent 2026 restructuring of the reduction formula is not detailed in tscer.md, so the exact mechanics are inferred rather than confirmed.

Its value (0.3821) equals $tscer_red_coef2 (0.4021) minus $tscer_red_coef3 (0.02), mirroring the same apparent calibration relationship. As with the related coef3/coef5 constants, tscer.md does not document this specific 2026-era formula, so the interpretation is inferred from the numeric pattern and the BenCalc parameter roles rather than confirmed by source text.

label.en: Contribution for labour unions and professional organizations

description.en: This constant is the employer contribution rate that funds labour unions and professional/employer organisations in France, expressed as a fraction of gross earnings (a 'whole income' base with no ceiling). It is used in policy tscer_fr's ArithOp function (Formula parameter, function comment 'Contribution to unions and professional organizations') to compute this specific employer social-contribution component. Both the country report (Table 2.58, 'Contribution to professional and unions organizations') and the FR contributions theme documentation confirm a rate of 0.016% of whole income, unchanged across 2022-2025, matching the constant's current value of 0.00016; only one rate change has ever been recorded since the earliest simulated system in 2006. It is one of many small levies that, alongside health, pension, family, housing and training contributions, make up total French employer social insurance contributions (tscer_s).

label.en: Unemployment insurance-lumps sum for white collar workers

description.en: This constant is labelled a fixed annual lump-sum amount ('currency/year') forming part of unemployment insurance contributions specifically for white-collar employees. It is defined and used within tscer_fr's BenCalc function (Comp_perTU parameter, function comment 'Unemployment insurance contributions'), where it would be added once per tax unit within the same formula that also combines the percentage-based unemployment insurance rates ($tscerui_rate1, $tscerui_rate2) and the wage guarantee fund rate ($tscerwgf_rate). Neither the country-report section on employer contributions nor the FR contributions theme documentation describes a separate flat-euro unemployment insurance charge for white-collar staff (cadres) -- French unemployment insurance and the APEC supplement are documented only as percentage rates -- and the constant's own value history (six recorded value periods since 2006) ends in 'n/a' for the latest system, suggesting this lump-sum component was applied historically but has since been discontinued or set inactive. Because the underlying legal basis could not be confirmed in the available sources, this description relies mainly on the constant's name, label and usage context.

label.en: Unemployment insurance contribution rate

description.en: This constant is the standard employer contribution rate for France's unemployment insurance scheme (assurance chômage, administered by Unédic/France Travail), applied to 'income group A+B' earnings (the broad gross-wage base used for this contribution). It is used in tscer_fr's BenCalc function (Comp_perTU parameter, function comment 'Unemployment insurance contributions'), combined in the same formula with the APEC supplement rate ($tscerui_rate2) and the wage guarantee fund rate ($tscerwgf_rate) to compute total unemployment-related employer contributions. The country report's Table 2.58 records the rate at 4.05% through 2022-2024 (falling to 4.00% from May in the 2025 system), and the FR contributions theme documentation confirms a flat 4% rate, consistent with the constant's current value of 0.04.

explanation.en: EUROMOD function group: Reduction coefficient

label.en: Unemployment insurance contribution rate-white collar supplement (APEC)

description.en: This constant is a supplementary employer unemployment-insurance contribution rate, levied on 'income group A+B' earnings, that funds APEC (Association Pour l'Emploi des Cadres), the French agency providing employment services for executives and managerial staff (cadres). It is used in tscer_fr's BenCalc function (Comp_perTU parameter, function comment 'Unemployment insurance contributions'), where it is combined with the base unemployment insurance rate ($tscerui_rate1) and related contributions within a single formula. Both the country report (Table 2.58, 'Agency for management employment (APEC)') and the FR contributions theme documentation confirm an employer APEC rate of 0.036% of income group A+B earnings, unchanged across 2022-2025, matching the constant's current value of 0.00036.

explanation.en: EUROMOD function group: Reduction coefficient

label.en: Wage guarantee fund - Income group A and B

description.en: This constant is the employer contribution rate for France's wage guarantee fund (AGS, Association pour la Gestion du régime de Garantie des créances des Salariés), which insures payment of employees' wages and related claims if their employer becomes insolvent; it applies to 'income group A and B' earnings and is paid entirely by employers. It is used in tscer_fr's BenCalc function (Comp_perTU parameter, function comment 'Unemployment insurance contributions'), bundled together with the unemployment-insurance and APEC rates within the same contribution formula, reflecting that these are collected jointly. The country report's Table 2.58 shows the rate rising from 0.15% (2022) to 0.20% (2024) to 0.25% (2025), and the FR contributions theme documentation confirms 0.25% as the current rate, matching the constant's latest value of 0.0025; the ten recorded value changes since 2006 reflect the fund's history of frequent rate adjustments.

label.en: Family contribution rate - artisans

description.en: $tscerfa_artisans_rate1 is the top marginal rate (3.1%) of the progressive family-benefits social contribution paid by self-employed artisans (and, per the shared Country Report table, industry-and-trade workers). It is used in tscse_fr/ArithOp as the Formula for 'Family Benefits-SIC' and as the Comp_UpLim in tscse_fr/BenCalc's 'Family Benefits-SIC (travailleurs indépendants)' function, i.e. the ceiling rate reached once income exceeds the applicable PSS-based threshold. The Country Report (tscse.md, Table 2.64) confirms this exact figure: self-employed income above 1.4×PSS is charged family-benefit contributions at 3.1%, with a linear ramp for income between 1.1×PSS and 1.4×PSS.

label.en: Family contribution rate-artisans with low incomes

Per the Country Report (tscse.md, Table 2.64), self-employed income at or below 1.1×PSS is exempt from the family-benefits contribution (0%), with the rate then rising linearly to the 3.1% ceiling ($tscerfa_artisans_rate1) as income approaches 1.4×PSS. This low rate functions as the exemption floor protecting lower-earning self-employed workers from the family-benefit charge.

The Country Report (tscse.md, Table 2.64) confirms this figure: artisans and industry-and-trade workers alike pay 1.3% of income below PSS for mandatory invalidity-and-death cover. This contribution funds disability and survivor benefits for self-employed artisans under the general self-employed social-security scheme.

label.en: Additional contribution

description.en: Rate of the French 'contribution additionnelle' (additional contribution), one of several separate social levies charged on investment and property (capital) income before their 2019 reform. Per the Country Report (Table 2.69), it stood at 0.30% in 2017 and 2018 and became not applicable (n/a) from 2019, when it was absorbed into the new consolidated 'solidarity levy' of 7.5% ($tsckt_solidaritylevy_rate). In the model it is used in policy tsckt_fr's ArithOp function (Formula parameter, commented "Liability"), together with $tsckt_social_rate and $tsckt_solidarity_rate, to compute the total social-contribution liability on capital income, simulated using observed current-year investment and property income; like the other capital-income levies it is not deductible for income tax purposes.

explanation.en: EUROMOD function group: Policy parameters

label.en: Social contribution

description.en: Rate of the French 'contribution sociale' (social contribution), one of the social levies applied to investment and property (capital) income before their 2019 consolidation. Per the Country Report (Table 2.69) it was 4.50% in 2017 and 2018; the five distinct values recorded since the policy's 2006 start in the model reflect earlier rate changes, before it too became not applicable (n/a) from 2019, when it was folded into the new unified 'solidarity levy' of 7.5% ($tsckt_solidaritylevy_rate). It is used, alongside $tsckt_addrate and $tsckt_solidarity_rate, in the Formula parameter of the ArithOp function in policy tsckt_fr (commented "Liability") that calculates the liability for this contribution on current-year capital income; the contribution is not deductible for tax purposes.

explanation.en: EUROMOD function group: Policy parameters

label.en: Solidarity contribution

description.en: Rate of the French 'contribution de solidarité' (solidarity contribution), another of the social levies applied to investment and property (capital) income before the 2019 reform. The Country Report (Table 2.69) shows it at 2.00% in 2017 and 2018, becoming not applicable (n/a) from 2019 when it was merged with the social and additional contributions into the new consolidated 'solidarity levy' of 7.5% ($tsckt_solidaritylevy_rate); the four distinct values recorded since 2006 reflect earlier changes to this rate. It feeds, together with $tsckt_social_rate and $tsckt_addrate, into the Formula parameter of tsckt_fr's ArithOp function (commented "Liability"), which computes the total liability on current-year investment and property income.

explanation.en: EUROMOD function group: Policy parameters

label.en: Solidarity levy

description.en: Rate of the French 'prélèvement de solidarité' (solidarity levy), the single consolidated social contribution on investment and property (capital) income that replaced the separate social, additional, and solidarity contributions from 2019. Per the Country Report (Table 2.69), it is set at 7.5% from 2019 onward (not applicable in the 2017-2018 period shown, consistent with its two recorded values), and combined with CSG and CRDS gives a total rate of 17.2% on capital income. It is used in policy tsckt_fr's ArithOp function (Formula parameter, commented "Liability") to compute the current-year contribution liability on observed investment and property income, alongside the now largely superseded $tsckt_social_rate, $tsckt_addrate and $tsckt_solidarity_rate constants.

label.en: CSG reduction threshold

description.en: Defines the annual earnings threshold, computed as four times the social-security ceiling ($PSS), above which the reduced CSG (Contribution Sociale Généralisée) assessment base of 98.25% of gross pay no longer applies and CSG is instead levied on the full 100% of gross income. It is used in tinty_fr's ArithOp function (Formula parameter, "Amount of CSG - earnings") and BenCalc function (Comp_perTU parameter, "Amount of CSG - unemployment benefits"), as well as the equivalent CSG-calculation functions in policy tscxc_fr. Theme_doc taxes.md confirms this exactly: the CSG base is "98.25% on gross income until four times the annual PSS, 100% above or for pension".

label.en: CSG reduction rate

description.en: The standard flat-rate reduction (1.75% of gross pay) applied before computing CSG (Contribution Sociale Généralisée) and CRDS (Contribution au Remboursement de la Dette Sociale) liabilities, representing a notional allowance for professional expenses on earnings and unemployment-benefit income. It is used extensively across the spine: in tinty_fr's ArithOp/BenCalc functions for CSG on earnings and unemployment benefits, in the equivalent functions of tscxc_fr, in tscdf_fr's ArithOp function (Formula parameter, "Liability") which computes CRDS, and in bsa00_fr's ArithOp function to "Calculate family work income" (likely approximating net-of-CSG earnings within the RSA resources test). Theme_doc taxes.md states the CSG/CRDS base is gross income "after a reduction of 1.75% for professional expenses ... on employment income and unemployment benefit", and cr:tscdf.md confirms CRDS is "paid on gross income after a reduction of 1.75% (3% until 2011)" - consistent with this constant's two recorded historical values.

label.en: Deduction for investment income

description.en: One of two fixed-amount allowances historically available against investment/dividend income ('revenus de capitaux mobiliers') in French personal income tax, applied on top of the proportional rebate ($tintadt_dedyiy_rate). It is used in tinty_fr's BenCalc function (comp_perTU parameter, "Deductions on investment income"). No current value is populated for this constant (raw "n/a") and neither the supplied theme_doc nor the CR excerpts describe this allowance in detail, so the description is inferred mainly from the constant's name, label and its pairing with $tintadt_dedyiy_amt2 and $tintadt_dedyiy_rate; it plausibly corresponds to a fixed dividend allowance that historically applied before being removed from French law, consistent with the constant no longer carrying a value in later systems.

label.en: Deduction for investment income

description.en: The second of two fixed-amount allowances historically available against investment/dividend income in French personal income tax, likely a single/couple counterpart to $tintadt_dedyiy_amt1, applied on top of the proportional rebate ($tintadt_dedyiy_rate). It is used in tinty_fr's BenCalc function (comp_perTU parameter, "Deductions on investment income"). As with $tintadt_dedyiy_amt1, no current value is populated (raw "n/a") and the supplied sources do not describe it in detail, so this description is based on the constant's name, label and usage context.

label.en: Deduction for investment income

description.en: The proportional rebate (40%) applied to dividend/investment income before it is added to taxable income under French personal income tax, used alongside the fixed-amount allowances ($tintadt_dedyiy_amt1/2); value 0.4, unchanged since 2006. It is used in tinty_fr's BenCalc function (comp_perTU parameter, "Deductions on investment income"). This is not detailed in the supplied theme_doc or CR excerpts; the description reflects the constant's name, label, and the well-established 40% dividend rebate that remains part of French tax law, unlike the related fixed allowances which appear to have been discontinued (both show no current value).

explanation.en: EUROMOD function group: Parameters for determining net taxable income (RNI)

label.en: Minimum deduction for private pension contributions

description.en: The minimum floor on the deductible amount for contributions to private/individual retirement savings plans against French personal income tax, applied even where 10% of prior earned income would otherwise produce a smaller figure; latest value €4,710, with 19 recorded historical values back to 2006. It is used in tinty_fr's BenCalc function (comp_lowlim parameter, "Tax deduction for private pension contributions"), together with the ceiling ($tintapv_uplim). Theme_doc taxes.md confirms: "Private retirement savings deduction: 10% of previous earned income (€4,710 to €37,680)", of which €4,710 is the floor.

label.en: Max deduction for private pension contributions

description.en: The ceiling on the deductible amount for private/individual retirement savings contributions against French personal income tax, capping the 10%-of-prior-earnings deduction; latest value €37,680, with 19 recorded historical values back to 2006. It is used in tinty_fr's BenCalc function (comp_uplim parameter, "Tax deduction for private pension contributions"), together with the floor ($tintapv_lowlim). Theme_doc taxes.md confirms the private retirement savings deduction range "(€4,710 to €37,680)", of which €37,680 is the ceiling.

label.en: Maximum deduction for earnings

description.en: The ceiling on the standard 10% professional-expenses deduction ($tintace_rate) applied to category-1 earned income (wages and salaries) in French personal income tax; latest value €14,555, with 20 recorded historical values back to 2006. It is used in tinty_fr's BenCalc function (comp_uplim parameter, "Tax deductions/ allowances for C1 income"), together with the rate and the floor ($tinty_ded_minamt). Theme_doc taxes.md confirms: "10% for earned income (€509 to €14,555)", of which €14,555 is the cap.

label.en: Minimum deduction for earnings

description.en: The floor on the standard 10% professional-expenses deduction for earned income, guaranteeing a minimum deduction even for low earners; latest value €509, with 17 recorded historical values. It is used in tinty_fr's BenCalc function (Comp_LowLim parameter, "Tax deductions/ allowances for C1 income"). Theme_doc taxes.md confirms the earned-income deduction range "(€509 to €14,555)", of which €509 is the floor.

label.en: Minimum deduction for unemployment benefits

description.en: The floor on the deduction applied to unemployment-benefit income within the same category-1 income tax treatment as earnings and pensions; the latest value is €0, meaning no guaranteed minimum deduction currently applies to unemployment benefits, in contrast to the positive floors that apply to earnings ($tinty_ded_minamt, €509) and pensions ($tinty_dedpens_minamt, €454). It is used in tinty_fr's BenCalc function (comp_lowlim parameter, "Tax deductions/ allowances for C1 income"). The supplied theme_doc gives only combined figures for earned income and pensions without breaking out unemployment benefits, so this description relies on the constant's name, label, and its parallel role to the earnings/pension floor constants; the 12 recorded historical values suggest this floor changed over time before being set to zero.

description.en: The ceiling on the 10%-style deduction applied to pension income in French personal income tax; latest value €4,439, with 19 recorded historical values back to 2006. It is used in tinty_fr's BenCalc function (comp_uplim parameter, "Tax deductions/ allowances for C1 income"). Theme_doc taxes.md confirms: "10% for ... pensions (€454 to €4,439)", of which €4,439 is the cap.

label.en: Minimum deduction for pension income

description.en: The floor on the 10%-style deduction applied to pension income, guaranteeing a minimum deduction for low pension amounts; latest value €454, with 17 recorded historical values. It is used in tinty_fr's BenCalc function (comp_lowlim parameter, "Tax deductions/ allowances for C1 income"). Theme_doc taxes.md confirms the pension deduction range "(€454 to €4,439)", of which €454 is the floor.

label.en: Maximum deduction for unemployment benefit

description.en: The ceiling on the deduction applied to unemployment-benefit income, the counterpart to $tinty_dedbun_lowlim; the latest value is €0, meaning the model currently applies no positive deduction cap specific to unemployment benefits. It is used in tinty_fr's BenCalc function (comp_uplim parameter, "Tax deductions/ allowances for C1 income"), playing the same structural role as $tinty_ded_maxamt (earnings) and $tinty_dedpens_maxamt (pensions) but for unemployment income. The supplied theme_doc does not break out unemployment benefits from earnings/pensions, so this description is based on name, label and usage context; the 13 recorded historical values indicate the cap changed over time before being zeroed.

label.en: Income limit for the deduction on property income

description.en: Sets the annual property/rental income ceiling (latest value €15,000/year, in force since 2006) that governs eligibility for a deduction on rental income within EUROMOD's tinty_fr policy. It is used twice in tinty_fr: in the Elig function (Elig_Cond) as the eligibility test that property income must not exceed this limit, and in the BenCalc function (Comp_Cond) as the condition defining the 'Deduction on rent income'. Neither the taxes theme document nor the tin.md country-report extract available for this batch describes this specific rental-income provision in detail, so the description relies mainly on the constant's name, label and model usage.

explanation.en: EUROMOD function group: Parameters for determining net taxable income (RNI)

used_by.function_comment: Income limit for the deduction on property income to apply

label.en: 1 share higher threshold for exemption

description.en: Represents the revenu-fiscal-de-référence (RFR) threshold for a household with one fiscal share ('part'), below which pension income is exempt from CSG (Contribution Sociale Généralisée); latest value €13,048/year, with 20 recorded values dating back to 2006. It is used together with $tscxc_thres2 (the per-additional-half-share increment) in tinty_fr's ArithOp (Formula), whose comment 'Calculate applicable threshold for exemption of pensions' shows it forms the base of a threshold that scales with the household's number of quotient-familial shares. This is consistent with the theme documentation's description of CSG on pension income as a rate 'that varies based on income' (Table 2.65), of which exemption is the lowest band.

explanation.en: EUROMOD function group: Parameters for determining net taxable income (RNI)

used_by.function_comment: Calculate applicable threshold for exemption of pensions

label.en: Each 0.5 share higher threshold for exemption

description.en: Represents the amount added to the base one-share threshold ($tscxc_thres1) for each additional half fiscal share ('demi-part') in a household, scaling the RFR (revenu fiscal de référence) exemption threshold for CSG on pension income to the size/composition of the tax unit; latest value €3,484/year, dating back to 2006. It is consumed alongside $tscxc_thres1 in the same tinty_fr ArithOp (Formula) annotated 'Calculate applicable threshold for exemption of pensions'. This reflects the French practice of scaling CSG income thresholds by the number of parts of the household's quotient familial, consistent with the CSG-on-pensions description in the theme documentation.

explanation.en: EUROMOD function group: Parameters for determining net taxable income (RNI)

used_by.function_comment: Calculate applicable threshold for exemption of pensions

label.en: 1 share higher threshold for reduced rate

description.en: Represents the RFR (revenu fiscal de référence) threshold for one fiscal share above which pension income moves out of the reduced ('taux réduit') CSG band; latest value €17,057/year, with 13 recorded values since 2006. It is used in tinty_fr's ArithOp (Formula) annotated 'Calculate applicable threshold for reduced rate for pensions', alongside $tscxc_thres4 which supplies the per-half-share increment. This is consistent with the theme documentation's note that the CSG rate on pensions 'varies based on income' (Table 2.65), the reduced rate being one of the intermediate bands between exemption and the full rate.

explanation.en: EUROMOD function group: Parameters for determining net taxable income (RNI)

used_by.function_comment: Calculate applicable threshold for reduced rate for pensions

label.en: Each 0.5 share higher threshold for reduced rate

description.en: Represents the amount added to the base one-share reduced-rate threshold ($tscxc_thres3) for each additional half fiscal share, so the CSG reduced-rate threshold for pension income scales with household composition; latest value €4,555/year, dating back to 2006. It is used together with $tscxc_thres3 in the tinty_fr ArithOp (Formula) commented 'Calculate applicable threshold for reduced rate for pensions'. As with the exemption-threshold pair, this reflects how French CSG income thresholds are expressed per 'part' of the quotient familial.

explanation.en: EUROMOD function group: Parameters for determining net taxable income (RNI)

used_by.function_comment: Calculate applicable threshold for reduced rate for pensions

label.en: 1 share higher threshold for median rate

description.en: Represents the RFR (revenu fiscal de référence) threshold for one fiscal share separating the median ('taux médian') CSG band from the top rate on pension income; latest value €26,472/year. Its time series holds only 9 recorded values (versus 20 for the exemption threshold and 13 for the reduced-rate threshold), suggesting this median-rate band was introduced later than the others. It is used in tinty_fr's ArithOp (Formula) commented 'Calculate applicable threshold for median rate for pensions', paired with $tscxc_thres6 for the per-half-share increment, consistent with the theme documentation's description of an income-varying CSG rate on pensions (Table 2.65).

explanation.en: EUROMOD function group: Parameters for determining net taxable income (RNI)

used_by.function_comment: Calculate applicable threshold for median rate for pensions

label.en: Each 0.5 share higher threshold for median rate

description.en: Represents the amount added to the base one-share median-rate threshold ($tscxc_thres5) for each additional half fiscal share, scaling the median-CSG-rate threshold for pension income to household composition; latest value €7,066/year, with 9 recorded values. It is used together with $tscxc_thres5 in the tinty_fr ArithOp (Formula) commented 'Calculate applicable threshold for median rate for pensions'. Like the exemption and reduced-rate threshold pairs, it reflects the 'part'-based scaling used throughout the French CSG-on-pensions rate structure noted in the theme documentation.

explanation.en: EUROMOD function group: Parameters for determining net taxable income (RNI)

used_by.function_comment: Calculate applicable threshold for median rate for pensions

label.en: Deductible CSG on capital income

description.en: A CSG (Contribution Sociale Généralisée) rate of 6.8% representing the portion of CSG levied on capital income that is deductible from taxable income for personal-income-tax purposes; in effect since 2006, with 3 recorded values in the series. It is used in tinty_fr's ArithOp (Formula) commented 'Amount of CSG - capital income' to compute this deductible CSG amount. The theme documentation confirms capital income is subject to CSG and that a deductible share exists 'from income before taxation', though it does not itemise the exact deductible/non-deductible split for capital income.

explanation.en: EUROMOD function group: Parameters for determining net taxable income (RNI)

classification.reason: CSG capital income deduction rate; decimal 0.068

label.en: Deductible CSG on sickness benefits

description.en: A CSG rate of 3.8% representing the deductible portion of CSG applied to a replacement-income benefit — labelled 'Deductible CSG on sickness benefits' in the model, though the function comment where it is actually applied describes it as calculating 'Amount of CSG - parental leave benefits'. It is used in tinty_fr's ArithOp (Formula), unchanged since 2006. This is broadly consistent with the theme documentation's statement that CSG is levied on sickness-type benefits and that 'deductibility varies by income type', though the specific rate and the label/usage mismatch are not resolved by the available source documents.

explanation.en: EUROMOD function group: Parameters for determining net taxable income (RNI)

used_by.function_comment: Amount of CSG - parental leave benefits

label.en: Deductible CSG on unemployment benefits

description.en: A CSG rate of 3.8% representing the portion of CSG on unemployment insurance benefits (allocation d'aide au retour à l'emploi) that is deductible from taxable income for personal-income-tax purposes; in force since 2006. It is used in tinty_fr's BenCalc (Comp_perTU) commented 'Amount of CSG - unemployment benefits' to compute this deductible CSG component per tax unit. The theme documentation lists a CSG rate of 6.2% on unemployment income (Table 2.65) and notes that CSG deductibility 'varies by income type', consistent with only part of that rate being deductible.

explanation.en: EUROMOD function group: Parameters for determining net taxable income (RNI)

label.en: Deductible CSG on pensions (reduced rate)

description.en: A CSG rate of 3.8% representing the deductible portion of CSG on pension income under the reduced ('taux réduit') rate band, applying to pensioners whose RFR falls between the exemption and reduced-rate thresholds ($tscxc_thres1-4). It is used in tinty_fr's BenCalc (Comp_perTU) commented 'Amount of CSG - pensions' to compute the deductible CSG amount per tax unit for this band. This is consistent with the theme documentation's note that the CSG rate on pensions 'varies based on income' (Table 2.65) and that a deductible share exists 'from income before taxation'.

explanation.en: EUROMOD function group: Parameters for determining net taxable income (RNI)

label.en: Deductible CSG on pensions (median rate)

description.en: A CSG rate of 4.2% representing the deductible portion of CSG on pension income under the median ('taux médian') rate band, applying to pensioners whose RFR falls between the reduced-rate and top-rate thresholds ($tscxc_thres5-6). It is used in the same tinty_fr BenCalc (Comp_perTU) function commented 'Amount of CSG - pensions' as the reduced- and normal-rate variants ($tscxcnkrd_dedpens_rate1/rate3), supplying the deductible CSG amount for this income band. This matches the theme documentation's description of an income-varying CSG rate on pensions (Table 2.65).

explanation.en: EUROMOD function group: Parameters for determining net taxable income (RNI)

label.en: Deductible CSG on pensions (normal rate)

description.en: A CSG rate of 5.9% representing the deductible portion of CSG on pension income at the normal ('taux normal', i.e. top) rate, applying to pensioners whose RFR exceeds the median-rate threshold ($tscxc_thres5-6). It is used in tinty_fr's BenCalc (Comp_perTU) commented 'Amount of CSG - pensions', alongside the reduced- and median-rate deductible variants, to compute the deductible CSG amount for the highest pension-income band. The theme documentation gives an overall CSG rate on pensions of around 8.3% that 'varies based on income' (Table 2.65), of which this constant represents the deductible share at the top band.

explanation.en: EUROMOD function group: Parameters for determining net taxable income (RNI)

label.en: Deductible CSG on earnings

description.en: A CSG rate of 6.8% representing the portion of CSG on employment earnings that is deductible from taxable income for personal-income-tax purposes, out of the total 9.2% CSG rate on employment income given in the theme documentation (Table 2.65). It is used in tinty_fr's ArithOp (Formula) commented 'Amount of CSG - earnings' to compute this deductible CSG amount. The theme documentation confirms CSG has a 'deductible share from income before taxation' and that deductibility 'varies by income type', consistent with only 6.8 of the 9.2 percentage points being deductible for earned income.

explanation.en: EUROMOD function group: Parameters for determining net taxable income (RNI)

label.en: Rate for contribution for solidarity and autonomy (CASA)

description.en: CASA (Contribution Additionnelle de Solidarité pour l'Autonomie) is a solidarity surtax on pension and survivor-pension income, introduced in 2013 to help fund old-age and disability autonomy support. In the FR spine it is applied within tscxc_fr's BenCalc function (parameter Comp_perTU, commented "Amount of CSG - pensions"), where it is added on top of the CSG due from pensioners whose CSG rate is at least the 6.6% median rate (it does not apply to those on the 3.8% reduced rate or exempted from CSG). Per the FR Country Report (section 2.6.4), the CASA rate is 0.3%, matching the constant's current value.

explanation.en: EUROMOD function group: Policy parameters

label.en: CSG normal rate on earnings

description.en: This is the standard ("normal") CSG rate applied to employment income, currently 9.2%. It is used in tscxc_fr's ArithOp function (parameter Formula, commented "Amount of CSG - earnings") to compute the CSG due on gross wages. Per the FR Country Report (section 2.6.4, Table 2.65), CSG on employment income is levied on a base equal to 98.25% of gross earnings (after the standard 1.75% deduction for professional expenses), and 6.8 of the 9.2 points are deductible from taxable income for personal income tax purposes.

explanation.en: EUROMOD function group: Policy parameters

label.en: CSG normal rate on pensions

description.en: The full ("normal") CSG rate applied to pension and survivor-pension income, currently 8.3%. It feeds into tscxc_fr's BenCalc function (parameter Comp_perTU, commented "Amount of CSG - pensions"), alongside the median (6.6%), reduced (3.8%) and CASA (0.3%) rates, to compute the CSG (and CASA) owed depending on the pensioner's reference income (RFR) band. Per the FR Country Report (section 2.6.4), this 8.3% rate was introduced for all pensioners in 2018, replacing the previous 6.6% rate, though lower-income pensioners have since been shielded via the median and reduced rates.

explanation.en: EUROMOD function group: Policy parameters

label.en: CSG normal rate on unemployment benefits

description.en: The standard CSG rate applied to unemployment insurance benefit (ARE), currently 6.2%. It is used in tscxc_fr's BenCalc function (parameter Comp_perTU, commented "Amount of CSG - unemployment benefits") to compute CSG due on unemployment benefits, levied on a base equal to 98.25% of the gross benefit (after the standard 1.75% deduction), per Table 2.65 of the FR Country Report (section 2.6.4). Low-income claimants may instead face a reduced/fully-deductible 3.8% rate or full exemption, which are handled by other constants.

explanation.en: EUROMOD function group: Policy parameters

label.en: CSG rate on capital income

description.en: CSG rate applied to capital/investment and property income; the constant's current modelled value is 10.6%, used in tscxc_fr's ArithOp function (parameter Formula, commented "Amount of CSG - capital income") to compute the CSG component of the social levies on capital income. Capital income in France is also subject to CRDS (0.5%) and an additional solidarity levy, together totalling a combined social-levy rate reported as 17.2% (rising to 17.2%-18.6% from 2026) in the FR taxes documentation; the Country Report's Table 2.65 separately lists a CSG-only capital-income figure of 9.2%, so the exact current split versus the modelled 10.6% could not be fully reconciled from the available sources.

explanation.en: EUROMOD function group: Policy parameters

label.en: CSG rate on sickness benefit

description.en: CSG rate applied to sickness-benefit-type daily allowances, currently 6.2% - the same rate that applies to unemployment benefits. Per Table 2.65 of the FR Country Report (section 2.6.4), CSG applies to "Sickness Benefit (only the daily allowances, not reimbursement for medical procedures)" at this 6.2% rate. In the FR spine the constant is actually consumed in tscxc_fr's ArithOp function (parameter Formula, commented "Amount of CSG - parental leave benefits"), i.e. it is applied to parental-leave daily allowances, which receive the same CSG treatment as sickness daily allowances under the replacement-income category.

explanation.en: EUROMOD function group: Policy parameters

used_by.function_comment: Amount of CSG - parental leave benefits

label.en: CSG median rate on pensions (from 2019)

description.en: An intermediate ("median") CSG rate of 6.6% on pension income, introduced in 2019 for pensioners whose reference income (RFR) falls in a middle band, shielding them from the full 8.3% rate introduced in 2018. It is used in tscxc_fr's BenCalc function (parameter Comp_perTU, commented "Amount of CSG - pensions") alongside the normal, reduced and CASA rates; the FR Country Report (section 2.6.4, Table 2.68) gives the RFR ceilings that determine eligibility for this median rate, by year and by number of household shares ("parts"). Pensioners on the 6.6% rate are also liable for the CASA surtax (0.3%).

explanation.en: EUROMOD function group: Policy parameters

label.en: CSG reduced rate on pensions

description.en: The reduced CSG rate of 3.8% on pension income, applied to pensioners whose reference income (RFR) is below the median-rate threshold but above the full-exemption threshold (Table 2.67 of the FR Country Report, section 2.6.4). Unlike the normal and median rates, this reduced rate is described as fully deductible from income for personal income tax purposes. It is used in tscxc_fr's BenCalc function (parameter Comp_perTU, commented "Amount of CSG - pensions") as one of the rate tiers applied depending on the pensioner's income band.

explanation.en: EUROMOD function group: Policy parameters

label.en: Base amount for the tax rebate (decote)

description.en: The base amount (single-taxpayer case) used to compute the décote, a non-refundable tax rebate that reduces gross income tax for low/moderate-liability tax units. It feeds Comp_perTU in the "Tax rebate (Decote)" BenCalc of both tin_fr and tinkt_fr, where the rebate equals this amount minus a fraction of gross tax liability (see $tin_decote_rate). It corresponds to the single-person row of the country report's Table 2.81 "tax rebate parameter for calculation", a series uprated roughly annually since 2006.

explanation.en: EUROMOD function group: Paramteres of the income tax

label.en: Base amount of decote for couples since 2015

description.en: The couple-specific base amount for the décote rebate calculation, in force since a 2015 reform gave jointly-taxed couples their own (higher) rebate formula distinct from the single-person case. Used alongside $tin_decote_amt as Comp_perTU in the "Tax rebate (Decote)" BenCalc of both tin_fr and tinkt_fr, and corresponds to the couple row of the country report's Table 2.81.

explanation.en: EUROMOD function group: Paramteres of the income tax

label.en: Limit for the tax rebate (decote) to apply

description.en: The ceiling on gross income tax liability (single-taxpayer case) below which a tax unit qualifies for the décote rebate at all. It is used as the Comp_Cond eligibility test in the "Tax rebate (Decote)" BenCalc of both tin_fr and tinkt_fr, and corresponds to the single row of the country report's Table 2.80 tax-rebate ceilings, which is uprated in step with the annual income-tax scale.

explanation.en: EUROMOD function group: Paramteres of the income tax

label.en: Higher threshold for decote for couples since 2015

description.en: The couple-specific ceiling on gross tax liability below which the décote applies, in force since the 2015 reform that gave couples their own higher rebate threshold. Used as Comp_Cond in the same "Tax rebate (Decote)" BenCalc functions of tin_fr and tinkt_fr as $tin_decote_lim1, and matches the couple row of the country report's Table 2.80.

explanation.en: EUROMOD function group: Paramteres of the income tax

label.en: Rate for decote

description.en: The factor (45.25%) subtracted, as a share of gross tax liability, when computing the décote rebate amount via Comp_perTU in the "Tax rebate (Decote)" BenCalc of tin_fr and tinkt_fr. According to the country report, this rate has applied since 2020, replacing a three-quarters (75%) factor used from 2017 to 2019, which explains the constant's short history of only a few recorded rate changes.

explanation.en: EUROMOD function group: Paramteres of the income tax

label.en: Value of the first 2 half shares for dependents in QF

description.en: A cap used in the "Plafonnement du quotient familial" (family-ratio capping) mechanism, which limits the tax saving generated by the additional half-shares (parts) granted for dependents in the quotient familial. It is used as Comp_perTU in tinkt_fr's BenCalc under "Imax: Limit on deductions claimed on behalf of dependents". Its value and the roughly annual uprating pattern seen in the model's dated series line up with the country report's Table 2.78 cap on the first two additional half-shares, though the report's wording ties that specific row to lone parents rather than dependents generally.

explanation.en: EUROMOD function group: Paramteres of the income tax

used_by.function_comment: Imax: Limit on deductions claimed on behalf of dependents

label.en: Value for the third share onwards for dependents in QF

description.en: The lower per-half-share cap applied within the same family-ratio-capping (Imax) mechanism as $tin_imaxdep_lim1, but for additional half-shares granted for dependents beyond the first two (i.e. from the third half-share onward). Used as Comp_perTU in tinkt_fr's BenCalc under "Imax: Limit on deductions claimed on behalf of dependents", consistent with the country report's Table 2.78 cap for each additional half-share after the second.

explanation.en: EUROMOD function group: Paramteres of the income tax

used_by.function_comment: Imax: Limit on deductions claimed on behalf of dependents

label.en: Complementary reduction for disabled for whom an imax correction applies

description.en: A further tax reduction ("réduction complémentaire") granted, on top of the family-ratio (Imax) correction, to each disabled person in the tax unit. Applied as Comp_perElig in the "Complementary reduction" BenCalc of both tin_fr and tinkt_fr. It corresponds to the "Disabled" row of the country report's Table 2.79, which lists this per-person reduction for tax units whose liability was already adjusted by the family-ratio cap.

explanation.en: EUROMOD function group: Paramteres of the income tax

label.en: Complementary reduction for widow/er with dependent child for whom an imax correction applies

description.en: A further tax reduction granted to widow(er)s with at least one dependent child, on top of the family-ratio (Imax) correction, applied as Comp_perElig in the same "Complementary reduction" BenCalc of tin_fr and tinkt_fr as $tin_imaxdis_amt. It matches the "Widower with dependent child" row of the country report's Table 2.79 complementary-reduction amounts.

explanation.en: EUROMOD function group: Paramteres of the income tax

label.en: Rate in band1

description.en: The 0% marginal rate on the lowest band of France's progressive personal income tax (Impôt sur le Revenu, IRPP). Used as Band_Rate both in tin_fr's SchedCalc to compute the "Gross income tax (before any IMAX corrections)" and again in tinkt_fr's SchedCalc to recompute tax under the reduced/floor quotient familial as part of the family-ratio-capping (Imax) mechanism. description.en: The flat withholding rate (12.8%) applied to capital income (interest, dividends and similar investment income) when taxed under the optional flat-rate regime instead of the progressive IRPP schedule. label.en: Additional amount for children aged 11-16

description.en: This constant defines an additional monthly amount per dependent child aged 11 to 16, forming part of the full-rate base amount of France's universal family benefit (Allocation Familiale, AF), computed in policy bch00_fr's BenCalc function via the Comp_perElig parameter (summed per eligible child, comment 'Benefit base amount (full rate)'). It has explicit values for only 6 dated periods starting 2006-01-01, and its latest value is recorded as 'n/a' (not currently populated): both the country report and the France benefits documentation describe today's AF structure as using a single 'over 14' age-related increment (extended to 'over 18' from March 2026) rather than an 11-16 bracket, suggesting this constant reflects an earlier, superseded design of the age-related supplement. Confidence is lowered because no source text explicitly discusses an 11-16 age bracket for this benefit.

explanation.en: EUROMOD function group: Constants

label.en: Additional base amount if child is over 14 (full rate)-FYA

description.en: This constant is the additional monthly amount added to the full-rate base amount of France's universal family benefit (Allocation Familiale, AF, policy bch00_fr) for each dependent child aged 14 or over, applied via the Comp_perElig parameter in bch00_fr's BenCalc function ('Benefit base amount (full rate)'). Per the country report, in two-child families this increment applies only to the second child (not the first), and since 1 July 2015 it has been subject to the same RFR-based (Revenu Fiscal de Reference) income test as the base AF amount. The '-FYA' (from-year-average) label reflects that the value blends amounts before and after mid-year uprating dates (e.g. the 4% increase applied on 1 July 2022); its latest value of 76.51 EUR/month matches the France 2025-2026 benefits documentation's figure for the 'over 14/18' increase in 2026.

explanation.en: EUROMOD function group: Constants

label.en: From: 2026: Additional amount for children aged over 18

description.en: This constant holds the additional monthly amount for children aged over 18, corresponding to a reform effective 1 March 2026 that extends France's family benefit (Allocation Familiale, AF) age-related increment from 'over 14' to 'over 18' for children born after 1 March 2012 (children born earlier retain the increase from age 14), per the France 2025-2026 benefits documentation. Its latest value, 76.51 EUR/month, is identical to the sibling constant $bch00_age14plus_amt, consistent with it being the forward-looking counterpart introduced for this reform. It currently has zero usage sites within bch00_fr (unused=true), meaning the value has been added to the parameter file but is not yet referenced by any BenCalc formula in the modelled policy spine -- the reform's parameter value is defined ahead of its logic being implemented.

explanation.en: EUROMOD function group: Constants

label.en: Base amount for families with 2 children (full rate)- FYA

description.en: This constant is the base full-rate monthly amount of France's universal family benefit (Allocation Familiale, AF) payable to a household with exactly 2 dependent children, applied once per tax unit via the Comp_perTU parameter in policy bch00_fr's BenCalc function ('Benefit base amount (full rate)'). It is uprated each 1 April: the country report's Table 2.6 records 151.81 EUR/month in 2025, and the France benefits documentation gives 153.01 for 2026, matching this constant's latest value, before any income-based reduction to 50% or 25% of the amount. The '-FYA' suffix indicates the figure is a from-year weighted average applied when an uprating occurs mid-year (e.g. the July 2022 increase).

explanation.en: EUROMOD function group: Constants

label.en: Income threshold to receive full rate for families with 2 children

description.en: This constant is the annual income ceiling, based on the household's Revenu Fiscal de Reference (RFR, n-2 reference fiscal income), below which a family with 2 dependent children receives France's universal family benefit (Allocation Familiale, AF) at the full rate. It is used in policy bch00_fr's BenCalc function via the Comp_Cond parameter ('Total benefit amount') when computing the total, means-tested benefit amount. The country report's Table 2.5 shows this threshold rising over time (e.g. 78,565 EUR in 2025), and the France benefits documentation gives 79,980 for 2026, matching this constant's latest value; households above it instead receive 50% (up to $bch00_child2_thres2) or 25% of the base amount, under the RFR-based means test introduced 1 July 2015.

explanation.en: EUROMOD function group: Constants

label.en: Income threshold to receive half rate for families with 2 children

description.en: This constant is the upper annual RFR income ceiling for 2-child families under France's universal family benefit (Allocation Familiale, AF): households with income between $bch00_child2_thres1 and this threshold receive AF at the half (50%) rate, while those above it receive only 25% of the base amount. It is used alongside $bch00_child2_thres1 in policy bch00_fr's BenCalc function via the Comp_Cond parameter ('Total benefit amount'), which computes the total means-tested benefit. The country report's Table 2.5 documents the equivalent 2025 threshold at 104,719 EUR; this constant's latest value of 106,604 EUR continues that year-on-year progression into 2026.

explanation.en: EUROMOD function group: Constants

label.en: Base amount for families with 3 children (full rate)- FYA

description.en: This constant is the base full-rate monthly amount of France's universal family benefit (Allocation Familiale, AF) payable to a household with exactly 3 dependent children, applied once per tax unit via the Comp_perTU parameter in policy bch00_fr's BenCalc function ('Benefit base amount (full rate)'), the same mechanism as $bch00_child2_amt for the 2-child case. The country report's Table 2.6 documents this amount rising from 308.26 EUR (2022) to 346.29 EUR (2025); this constant's latest value of 349.06 EUR/month for 2026 continues that uprating trend, though the exact 2026 figure is not separately itemised in the France benefits documentation's summary table. As with the 2-child amount, the '-FYA' label indicates a from-year weighted average is used across mid-year uprating dates.

label.en: Income threshold to receive full rate for families with 3 children

description.en: This constant is the annual RFR (Revenu Fiscal de Reference) income ceiling below which a household with 3 dependent children receives France's universal family benefit (Allocation Familiale, AF) at the full rate, used in policy bch00_fr's BenCalc function via the Comp_Cond parameter ('Total benefit amount') for the total means-tested benefit. The France benefits documentation gives this threshold as 86,644 EUR for 2026 (up from 85,111 EUR in 2025 per the country report's Table 2.5), matching this constant's latest value exactly. Households above this ceiling move into the 50% or 25% rate bands (see $bch00_child3_thres2).

label.en: Additional base amount per each 20 year old child for families with 3 or more children (full rate)- FYA

description.en: This constant is a fixed monthly lump-sum top-up paid within France's universal family benefit (Allocation Familiale, AF) to families with 3 or more children when a qualifying child is aged 20, applied via the comp_perTU parameter in policy bch00_fr's BenCalc function, described in the model as the 'extra benefit amount given to families with 3+ children and a child aged 20'. Per the country report, this requires the 20-year-old to live at home and either not work or earn under 55% of the minimum wage (SMIC, on a 169-hour/month basis), and requires that the family already received AF for 3+ children the month before that child's 20th birthday; it is paid monthly until the month before the child turns 21, and EUROMOD simulates it for the full year whenever a non-head/partner 20-year-old lives with at least two dependent children. Its latest value, 96.75 EUR/month, matches the France benefits documentation's 2026 figure for large families with an eldest child aged 20-21, continuing the country report's Table 2.6 series (95.99 EUR in 2025).

description.en: This constant is the annual increment added to the household's RFR income threshold for each dependent child beyond the third, used in policy bch00_fr's BenCalc function via the Comp_Cond parameter ('Total benefit amount') to scale up the means-test thresholds for larger families when computing France's universal family benefit (Allocation Familiale, AF). The country report's Table 2.5 documents this increase rising from 5,839 EUR (2022) to 6,546 EUR (2025); this constant's latest value of 6,664 EUR/year matches the France benefits documentation's explicit 2026 figure ('thresholds increase by 6,664 EUR per additional child').

label.en: tax credit equal to 50% of childcares expenses, within an annual cap

description.en: Represents the rate of the French personal income tax credit for childcare expenses incurred outside the home, expressed here in percentage-point terms (unit /100); its value of 50% from 2024 reflects that parents can reclaim half of qualifying childcare costs as a non-refundable tax credit. Although this particular rate parameter is defined in the childcare-costs policy xcc_fr for the more recent systems, it feeds into tintcot_fr's BenCalc function (Comp_perElig parameter, "Tax credit on child care expenses") within the personal income tax module. Theme_doc taxes.md confirms the rule: childcare fees give a credit of "50% of expenses, up to €3,500 per child", which cannot be combined with other childcare deductions.

label.en: Low Lim Hourly rate: 1 child

description.en: This is the floor (minimum) hourly parental contribution rate, in euros, that a household with exactly one dependent child must pay for centre-based childcare (crèche) in France, however low its income-based hourly fee would otherwise be. It is used in the xcc_fr policy's BenCalc function, in the Comp_perTU component commented 'Low Lim Hourly rate', to bound the income-related hourly fee for the one-child band before it is scaled up (assuming 40 hours/week full-time care) into the household-level monthly gross childcare-fee variable xcc_s (tu_household_fr). Per the childcarecost documentation this floor is €0.50 per hour, unchanged between the 2025 and 2026 system years, and it is one part of the family-size-related fee reduction described alongside the ceiling rates.

description.en: $bdi_amt1 is the maximum/basic monthly amount of the AAH (Allocation aux Adultes Handicapés) disability benefit modelled by bdi_fr. In bdi_fr/BenCalc it is used as the Comp_UpLim cap (comment "Benefit amount") on the differential benefit component, i.e. it ceils the formula AAH = (income threshold − income)/12 at the full-rate amount. Per the Country Report (Table 2.24, "Maximum Monthly benefit") and benefits.md, this ceiling has risen from about €920 in 2022 to €1,041.59 by 2026, uprated annually (with a mid-year 4% increase applied on 1 July 2022 via the FYA mechanism).
