description.en: $bdi_amt2 is the flat monthly "increase for independent living" (Majoration pour la vie autonome) supplement to the AAH disability benefit. It is added in bdi_fr/BenCalc as a Comp_perTU component (comment "Supplement for independent living") on top of the basic AAH amount. Per the Country Report (Table 2.25) and benefits.md, it is awarded to AAH recipients paid at the full rate (or as a complement to an old-age/invalidity pension) who report no work income, and has been stable at €104.77/month since 2022; the EUROMOD modelling note states it is simulated for full-rate AAH recipients and for those reporting zero earnings, since the degree of disability is not observed in the data.

description.en: Sets the annual individual income threshold (based on income from two years prior, n-2) that a partner in a couple must earn to be counted as an 'earner' for the PAJE-base and Family Complement income tests; couples where both partners fall below this amount are treated as a one-earner couple and assessed against the lower one-earner income ceiling rather than the higher two-earner ceiling. Although defined in bchyc_fr, it is shared across two benefits: it feeds the eligibility condition of bchyc_fr's Elig function (used to classify one-earner couples, married or cohabiting) for the PAJE base (Allocation de base), and the income-test condition of bchlg_fr's BenCalc (which counts earning partners in the unit) for the means-tested Family Complement (Complement familial). The country report's Tables 2.7 and 2.18 give this threshold as EUR 5,983 for 2025 (based on 2023 income); the model's current value of EUR 6,306 matches the theme description's 2026 update, 'the n-2 income must be > EUR 6,306'.

description.en: Holds the current full monthly PAJE-base (Allocation de base) rate for children born on or after 1 April 2018, used once as the per-tax-unit amount (Comp_perTU) in bchyc_fr's BenCalc. Per the constant's own label, this formula cell is invoked for households whose n-2 income lies between ceiling C2 and ceiling C1 -- the band in which, per the country report, only a reduced 50% share of the full rate is actually paid, so the halving is presumably applied by the surrounding formula rather than baked into this constant. Its value tracks the country report's Table 2.10 'full rate' row year by year (185.74 in 2023, 194.28 in 2024, 197.59 in 2025) and stands at 199.16 EUR/month for 2026; the 'FYA' (Full Year Adjustment) tag in the label reflects that for 2022, when the rate rose mid-year on 1 July, the model instead stored a weighted full-year average of the pre- and post-increase amounts, as the country report describes for this benefit.

description.en: $bchba_amt1 holds the flat-rate PAJE 'Prime de naissance' (birth/adoption grant) amount that applied under the pre-reform rules, i.e. before the 1 April 2018 change (the label notes the policy's internal switch points at 1 April 2014 and March 2018). It is used once, in bchba_fr's ArithOp function (Formula parameter, 'Benefit: Amount' comment) in the base EUROMOD spine, to supply the per-child lump sum for periods before the model switches to the post-2018 rate held in $bchba_amt2. Per the France country report, this means-tested grant (income thresholds set out in Table 2.11) is paid for each child born or adopted in the year, is not taxable but is subject to CRDS, and is compatible with other child benefits; only childbirth (not adoption) is actually simulated. The parameter's own value series ends before the current parameter vintage (raw_latest 'n/a'), and neither the theme doc nor the country report gives the exact pre-2018 euro figures, so the specific historical amount is not confirmed from these sources.

It feeds the bchcc_fr policy's BenCalc function as the Comp_perTU value of the 'PreParE Majorée: amount' component, added once per tax unit when a family with three or more children opts for this scheme (available for at most 8 months per parent, or 12 months for lone parents, before the child's first birthday, subject to the same 8-quarters social-security-contribution test as standard PreParE). description.en: $bched_lim1 is the annual net taxable income ceiling used in the ARS (Allocation de rentrée scolaire) means test for households with exactly one dependent child. It is used in bched_fr's BenCalc via the Comp_perTU parameter (comment 'Eligibility: Calculate applicable income threshold'), computed once per tax/benefit unit to set the threshold that household income is compared against for eligibility, and (since 2012) as the base of the 'ARS différentielle' formula for households whose income slightly exceeds the ceiling. Per the country report and the benefits theme document this threshold is set at 28,956 EUR for 2026 (up from 28,444 EUR in 2025); a one-child household must have net taxable income below it to receive the benefit, with $bched_lim2 and $bched_lim3 giving the analogous thresholds for households with two or three children.

description.en: This constant is the lower limit of the first taxable band of twl_fr, EUROMOD's model of the pre-2018 French general net-wealth tax (impôt de solidarité sur la fortune, ISF), used as the Band_LowLim parameter in twl_fr/SchedCalc to build the progressive rate scale. When active in this model (2013-2017), this threshold marked the entry point above which net taxable wealth began to fall into the first taxed band. Its value is currently n/a because ISF was abolished from 2018 and replaced by the real-estate-only wealth tax modelled separately as trewl_fr (IFI). This is not covered by the supplied 'taxes' theme note, which documents only currently-active taxes, so confidence rests on the constant's name, usage, and general knowledge of the ISF reform.

Fixed euro term (€17,500 in the single period it was defined, 2013-2017) in a 'décote' (tapering relief) formula that the twl_fr/ArithOp Formula parameter uses together with $twl_smoothing_rate to soften the transition into wealth-tax liability for households whose net taxable wealth sits just above the $twl_threshold entry point, avoiding a cliff-edge jump into full taxation. It corresponds to the fixed term of the relief formula for the pre-2018 French net wealth tax (Impôt de Solidarité sur la Fortune, ISF) set out in Article 885 U of the Code général des impôts: relief equalled this amount minus $twl_smoothing_rate times net taxable wealth, for wealth between the €1.3m liability threshold and €1.4m. The constant is n/a before 2013 and from 2018 onward because ISF was abolished from 2018 and replaced by the real-estate-only wealth tax modelled separately in trewl_fr (Impôt sur la Fortune Immobilière); this historical tax predates the current 2025-2026 taxes theme note and is not discussed there.

description.en: Proportional rate (1.25%, i.e. 0.0125, in the single period it was defined, 2013-2017) used alongside $twl_smoothing_amount in the twl_fr/ArithOp Formula parameter to compute the 'décote' relief that phases the wealth tax in gradually for households just above the $twl_threshold entry point, rather than imposing full liability the instant the threshold is crossed. It is the proportional term of the relief formula for the pre-2018 French net wealth tax (Impôt de Solidarité sur la Fortune, ISF), Article 885 U of the Code général des impôts: relief = $twl_smoothing_amount minus this rate times net taxable wealth, applicable to wealth between the €1.3m liability threshold and €1.4m. The constant is n/a outside 2013-2017 because ISF was abolished from 2018 and replaced by the real-estate-only wealth tax modelled in trewl_fr (IFI); it predates and is not covered by the current 2025-2026 taxes theme note.

description.en: Net-wealth liability threshold (€1,300,000 in the single period it was defined, 2013-2017) used as the Elig_Cond parameter in twl_fr/Elig to determine which units are simulated as owing the twl_fr wealth tax at all: only households with net taxable wealth at or above this level are treated as liable. It matches the assujettissement threshold of the French net wealth tax (Impôt de Solidarité sur la Fortune, ISF) as it stood from 2013: the tax's rate scale nominally started at a lower bracket (€800,000), but no tax was actually due until total net wealth reached €1.3m, creating a threshold effect that $twl_smoothing_amount and $twl_smoothing_rate then smoothed for wealth between €1.3m and €1.4m. ISF was abolished from 2018 and replaced by trewl_fr (Impôt sur la Fortune Immobilière, a real-estate-only wealth tax), so this constant has no value in later systems and is not covered by the 2025-2026 taxes theme note, which documents only the present-day tax system.

description.en: This constant is the €1,300,000 entry threshold of the progressive net-taxable-wealth scale used by trewl_fr, EUROMOD's model of the French real-estate wealth tax (impôt sur la fortune immobilière, IFI), which has taxed households' net real estate assets above this level since it replaced the broader ISF wealth tax in 2018. It is used in trewl_fr/BenCalc as the Comp_Cond parameter of a function tagged 'Tax schedule', defining the bracket boundary at which the first marginal rate ($trewl_rate1) begins to apply. Together with $trewl_bracket2 (€1,400,000) it also frames the 'décote' smoothing zone that softens the entry into taxation for households whose wealth is only just above the threshold. This tax falls outside the scope of the supplied 'taxes' theme note, which covers only IRPP/CSG/CRDS-type levies, so the description relies on the constant's value pattern, its usage, and general knowledge of the French wealth-tax reform.

This constant is the €1,400,000 threshold of the trewl_fr real-estate wealth tax (IFI) scale, forming the upper bound of the smoothing ('décote') band that starts at $trewl_bracket1 (€1,300,000) and reduces the tax due for households whose net taxable real estate wealth is only just above the entry threshold, avoiding a sharp jump in liability. It is used in trewl_fr/BenCalc as a Comp_Cond bracket-boundary parameter of the 'Tax schedule' function, alongside the corresponding rate constant $trewl_rate2. This is not documented in the supplied 'taxes' theme note, which does not cover wealth tax, so this reading is based on the value pattern and general knowledge of the IFI décote mechanism.

description.en: This is P0forf, the fixed monthly floor for the minimal personal participation P0 in the AL/APL housing-benefit formula (Pp = P0 + Tp*Rp, where Pp is the tenant's minimal personal participation). In bhotn_fr it is used as the LowLim of an ArithOp whose Formula computes 8.5%*(L+C) (func_comment: '(Pp) Personal participation rate - P0'), implementing Equation 5 of the Country Report, P0 = Max(P0forf, 8.5%*(L+C)), so the household's participation floor never falls below this amount. The Country Report's Table 2.39 gives P0forf as €39.56/month from October 2025, up from €35.39 at the start of 2022, uprated in the same rounds (July 2022, then each October) as the other AL/APL parameters. The constant's own EUROMOD label ('Annual increase') does not describe its role; its value and ArithOp usage identify it as the P0forf floor.

It is used in bhotn_fr's BenCalc function (parameter Comp_perTU, step '(L) Calculate applicable rent limit') to cap the actual rent used in the calculation. label.en: Rate: min rate for 0-45

description.en: The intercept ('rate min') term for the lowest bracket (RL between 0% and 45%) of the three-part schedule used to compute Tl, one of the two components (with Tf) of the personal participation rate Tp in the French housing-benefit formula (Pp = P0 + Tp×Rp). It is used in bhotn_fr's BenCalc function (Comp_perTU, '(Pp) Personal participation rate - Rate Min'), alongside the matching marginal rate $bho_rl_rate1, to express the piecewise Tl schedule of Table 2.42 of the France country report in linear (rate×RL − rate_min) form. Its value is 0, consistent with Table 2.42 setting Tl = 0% for RL between 0-45%, i.e. no participation-rate addition in this first bracket.

used_by.function_comment: Benefit Amount: (Pp) Personal participation rate - Rate Min

label.en: Rate: min rate for 45-75

description.en: The intercept ('rate min') term for the middle bracket (RL between 45% and 75%) of the three-part schedule used to compute Tl, one of the two components (with Tf) of the personal participation rate Tp in the French housing-benefit formula (Pp = P0 + Tp×Rp). It is used in bhotn_fr's BenCalc function (Comp_perTU, '(Pp) Personal participation rate - Rate Min') together with the marginal rate $bho_rl_rate2 (0.45) so Tl can be computed as rate×RL − rate_min instead of rate×(RL−45%). Its value, 0.2025, equals 0.45 (the rate) × 0.45 (the 45% bracket boundary expressed as a fraction), consistent with Table 2.42 of the France country report's formula Tl = 0.45%*(RL-45%) for this bracket.

label.en: Rate: min rate for >75

description.en: The intercept ('rate min') term for the top bracket (RL above 75%) of the three-part schedule used to compute Tl, one of the two components (with Tf) of the personal participation rate Tp in the French housing-benefit formula (Pp = P0 + Tp×Rp). It is used in bhotn_fr's BenCalc function (Comp_perTU, '(Pp) Personal participation rate - Rate Min') together with the marginal rate $bho_rl_rate3 (0.68) so Tl can be computed in linear (rate×RL − rate_min) form. Its value, 0.375, is consistent with Table 2.42 of the France country report's formula Tl = 0.45%*30% + 0.68%*(RL-75%) for RL above 75% (0.68×0.75 − 0.45×0.30 = 0.375).

label.en: Income limit for single person- FYA

description.en: Monthly income/resource ceiling used to compute the Allocation de solidarité aux personnes âgées (ASPA, "minimum vieillesse", solidarity allowance for the elderly) for a single claimant. ASPA is a differential benefit equal to this maximum amount minus one third of the claimant's quarterly family income (floored at zero), so the constant simultaneously represents both the eligibility income cap and the maximum monthly ASPA payment for a single person with no other resources. It is used in the bsaoa_fr policy's BenCalc function via the Comp_perTU parameter, which computes the benefit amount per tax unit; eligibility additionally requires the claimant to be aged 65 or over, retired, with the income test excluding family and housing benefits. The "FYA" (Full Year Adjustments) tag in the label indicates this value is a weighted average of the amounts in force before and after any within-year uprating (e.g. the 4% increase applied on 1 July 2022), weighted by the number of months each amount applied, rather than the single 30-June snapshot EUROMOD uses by default; the latest value (1043.59) corresponds to the amount reported as taking effect in 2026, up from 1034.28 in 2025.

label.en: Income limit for couples - FYA

description.en: Monthly income/resource ceiling used to compute the Allocation de solidarité aux personnes âgées (ASPA, "minimum vieillesse", solidarity allowance for the elderly) for a couple, applied when at least one partner is aged 65 or over. ASPA is a differential benefit equal to this maximum amount minus one third of the couple's quarterly family income (floored at zero), so the constant is both the couple eligibility income cap and the maximum monthly ASPA payment when the couple has no other resources; income considered excludes family and housing benefits and covers only the beneficiary and partner. It is used in the bsaoa_fr policy's BenCalc function via the Comp_perTU parameter, alongside the single-person ceiling ($bsaoa_amt1), to compute the benefit amount per tax unit. The "FYA" (Full Year Adjustments) tag indicates the value is a weighted average of the amounts before and after any within-year uprating (weighted by the number of months each applied) rather than the standard 30-June snapshot; the latest value (1620.18) corresponds to the amount reported as taking effect in 2026, up from 1605.73 in 2025.

label.en: Family minimum - Pregnant without child (not used)

description.en: One of four family-composition tiers of the monthly "family minimum" (montant forfaitaire) used by bchlp_fr, EUROMOD's implementation of France's former means-tested lone-parent benefit, the Allocation de Parent Isolé (API, pre-dating the RSA). This tier was the base amount for a pregnant claimant with no children yet (€566.79/month in FR_2008, the last year the amount was populated); it is tagged "not used" because bchlp_fr's own BenCalc explicitly notes that amounts for pregnant women are not simulated (no pregnancy indicator in the micro-data), hence 0 usage sites. The whole bchlp_fr policy — and this constant — has been switched to "n/a" (dormant) in every system from FR_2009 onward, since the API was abolished and folded into the RSA when it was rolled out nationally in June 2009.

explanation.en: EUROMOD function group: Constants

label.en: Family minimum - One dependent child

description.en: Monthly family-minimum floor for an Allocation de Parent Isolé (API) claimant — a lone parent or pregnant person with a young child — with exactly one dependent child, feeding BenCalc's Comp_perTU parameter in bchlp_fr's "Eligibility: Calculate applicable family minimum" function, which builds the intermediate variable temp_bchlp_mininc used later as the benefit's starting amount. In the last year API was active (FR_2008) it was set at €755.72/month, up from €735.75 in 2006; both the constant and the wider bchlp_fr policy have carried the value "n/a" (switched off) in every system since FR_2009, when the API was absorbed into the RSA.

Its last populated value was €944.65/month in FR_2008; like the rest of the API-related constants it has been "n/a" (the policy switched off) in every system since FR_2009, when the API was merged into the RSA.

Its last populated value was €188.93/month in FR_2008; the constant has been "n/a" since FR_2009 along with the rest of the (now defunct) API policy.

It is unused for the same reason as the matching family-minimum tier ($bchlp_fm_amt01): the model does not simulate this benefit for pregnant women. Its last populated value was €53.75/month (FR_2008); the constant and the wider policy have been dormant ("n/a") since FR_2009 when the API was absorbed into the RSA.

Its last populated value was €107.50/month (FR_2008); it has been "n/a" (policy switched off) in every system since FR_2009, when the API was folded into the RSA.

label.en: Rate

description.en: $tscdf_fullrate is the flat statutory rate of the CRDS (Contribution pour le Remboursement de la Dette Sociale — the social security debt repayment contribution), set to 0.5% (0.005) in every EUROMOD FR system since 2006. It is used in tscdf_fr's 'Liability' ArithOp to compute the CRDS due, applied on the same broad income base as CSG (employment, self-employment, pension, unemployment/activity-allowance income, family benefits, capital income, housing benefits and sickness daily allowances), generally after the same abatement as CSG (e.g. levied on 98.25% of gross pension/capital/sickness income up to four times the annual PSS, 100% above), and, unlike CSG, family benefits are also subject to CRDS. The same rate is also referenced in bsa00_fr's 'Calculate family work income' ArithOp, where it is used to net CRDS out of gross work income so as to approximate the net taxable/net social income figure that the RSA (Revenu de Solidarité Active) means test relies on. CRDS is not deductible for income-tax purposes.

label.en: Maximum amount for single person without children- FYA (weighted average)

description.en: This is the maximum monthly RSA ('Revenu de Solidarité Active') lump-sum amount for a single adult with no dependent children — the base tier of the benefit's household-composition scale. It feeds policy bsa00_fr's BenCalc function via the Comp_perTU parameter, which sets the household's maximum-income ceiling in the RSA formula: RSA = (maximum income by household composition) − (quarterly household income/3 + housing package), as described in the FR country report's RSA section. The '(weighted average)' in its label reflects EUROMOD's FYA mechanism, under which a year containing a mid-year revalorisation (e.g. the 4% increase applied from 1 July 2022) is represented as an income-weighted average of the pre- and post-increase rates. Its current value, €651.69/month, matches the 2026 single-person RSA rate reported in the FR benefits summary.

It is used in bsa00_fr's BenCalc via the comp_perElig parameter, adding one increment per qualifying additional child to the household's maximum RSA income. The constant's own label notes that before 2009 this specific majored per-child top-up was not simulated in EUROMOD (since API eligibility only stacked with one of the related allowances at the time) and that its value was historically pegged to 30 June; currently it is €278.95/month, about 7% above the equivalent non-majored increment ($bsa00_amt4, €260.68).

label.en: Applicable housing package to be deducted: single person-  FYA

description.en: This is the monthly 'housing package' (forfait logement) deducted for a single person with no children when computing the French Activity Allowance (Prime d'activité). Per the country report, it equals 12% of the allowance's flat-rate reference amount ('montant forfaitaire'/lump sum, $bsawk_minamt) — 76.59 EUR/month corresponds to 12% of the 2026 lump sum (638.28 EUR). It is used in bsawk_fr's BenCalc function (Comp_perTU parameter) to compute the housing package subtracted from the maximum benefit in the allowance formula: Allowance = (Maximum minimum income + a share of family work income + Bonus) − (max(household resources; maximum minimum income) + Housing package). The 'FYA' suffix marks it as the weighted-average value used by the model's FYA extension when the underlying rate changes mid-year (as in July 2022).

It feeds into bsawk_fr's BenCalc function (Comp_perTU parameter) as the amount netted off the household's maximum Activity Allowance entitlement. Labelled FYA, it is the system-year weighted-average figure used when the housing package rate is revalued mid-year.

label.en: Maximum minimum income (montant forfaitaire)- Single Without children- FYA (Weighted Average)

description.en: This is the base flat-rate reference amount ('montant forfaitaire') of the French Activity Allowance (Prime d'activité) for a single adult without children — the 'lump sum' quoted in the country report's Table 2.30 (633.21 EUR in 2025, rising to 638.28 EUR in 2026 per the FR benefits description). It is central to the benefit's design: bsawk_fr's ArithOp function (Formula parameter) uses it to compute the individual work bonus, which since 2019 is capped at 29.101% of this lump sum, while bsawk_fr's BenCalc function (Comp_Cond parameter) checks it is set/positive as part of the sorting logic feeding the BTA (non-take-up) and BCA (calibration) extensions. All the other household-composition 'minamt'/'hp_amt' constants in bsawk_fr are derived as percentage multiples of this base value.

It is used in bsawk_fr's BenCalc function (Comp_perTU parameter) to set the family's maximum-benefit/resource-disregard threshold in the allowance formula ('Allowance = Maximum minimum income + ... − max(resources; Maximum minimum income) − Housing package'). It is used in bsawk_fr's BenCalc function (Comp_perTU parameter) as the maximum-benefit/resource-disregard threshold for this household type. description.en: This is the incremental amount added to the Activity Allowance ceiling for each additional dependent child (or person under 25) beyond the second, equal to 40% of the base lump sum (638.28 × 0.4 ≈ 255.31 EUR/month) — the country report's uplift rate for household members beyond the third person where the household has more than 2 dependent children/persons under 25. Unlike the other household-composition constants, it is applied via bsawk_fr's BenCalc function (Comp_perElig parameter, not Comp_perTU), meaning it is added once per additional eligible child rather than looked up once per family type. It represents the marginal per-child top-up to the 'maximum minimum income' used in sizing the benefit for larger families.

description.en: Flat per-tax-unit amount of bsaeccm_fr, EUROMOD's implementation of a one-off French Covid-19 social-assistance top-up that the policy's own comment says was "given twice in May and November 2020" to recipients of the RSA, the ASS unemployment assistance, or APL housing benefit. It feeds BenCalc's Comp_perTU in the policy's "Benefit calculation" function ("Benefit for RSA recipients" / "for ASS recipients if not RSA" / "for APL recipients if not RSA nor ASS" groups); in the only year it was active (FR_2020) it was coded as the formula "150*2", i.e. €150 paid on each of the two 2020 rounds (€300 for the year), and it has been "n/a" (policy switched off) in every system from FR_2021 onward.

label.en: Annual amount for gross income≤ 23700€ per year

description.en: This constant is the euro lump sum paid under France's 2023 exceptional purchasing-power bonus for public servants (indemnité inflation, policy binps_fr) to eligible employees whose gross remuneration over the reference period 1 July 2022-30 June 2023 was at or below €23,700 (annualised to a full 12-month equivalent where the employment period was shorter). In the model it is the Comp_perElig value of the first component of the binps_fr/BenCalc function, added once per eligible tax-unit member whose income satisfies the matching Comp_Cond condition bounded by $binps_lim1. Per Décret n° 2023-702 du 31 juillet 2023, this is the top tier of the seven-band scale, worth €800, paid as a single lump sum in the last quarter of 2023 (prorated for part-time work or periods of employment under 12 months) and subject to social contributions and income tax.

It feeds into binps_fr/BenCalc as the Comp_perElig value of the second component, added once per eligible unit member whose income satisfies that band's Comp_Cond. Per Décret n° 2023-702 du 31 juillet 2023 this tier is worth €700, part of the seven-step scale (€800 down to €300) used to pay the one-off bonus in the last quarter of 2023, prorated for part-time or partial-year employment and subject to social contributions and income tax.

In binps_fr/BenCalc it is used in the Comp_Cond condition of the first component to test whether an eligible employee's income qualifies for the €800 lump sum ($binps_amt1). Per Décret n° 2023-702 du 31 juillet 2023, public servants whose annualised gross remuneration is at or below this threshold receive the top tier of the seven-band scale.

It is one of the twelve household-composition/RFR amount cells fed into bhoey_fr/BenCalc's Comp_perTU, the component whose comment notes that the benefit amount is based on household composition and on the RFR. label.en: Tax rates

description.en: This constant is the tax rate applied to compute France's recurrent local property tax on built/developed real estate (taxe foncière sur les propriétés bâties, TFPB), currently 30.62% (0.3062). It is used in tpr_fr/BenCalc as the Comp_perTU parameter, multiplying a taxable base approximating the cadastral rental value of built property to derive each tax unit's liability. In reality TFPB rates are set independently by each commune, intercommunality and département and vary widely, so this constant likely represents a single simplified/average national rate. The supplied 'taxes' theme note does not cover property tax, so this reading rests on the constant's name, its 'Tax rates' label, and its usage site.

This is the counterpart tax rate for the property tax on non-built/undeveloped land (taxe foncière sur les propriétés non bâties, TFPNB), paired with $tpr_rate_baties for built property, and used in the same tpr_fr/BenCalc computation (Comp_perTU parameter) that derives the property-tax liability per tax unit. Its current value is 0, meaning EUROMOD does not currently levy any simulated tax on non-built property, unlike the still-active built-property rate. No label or theme-note coverage is available for this constant, so the description is inferred from its name, its shared usage site with $tpr_rate_baties, and general knowledge of France's dual built/non-built property tax structure.

label.en: Thresholds for total exemption

description.en: This is the base annual income threshold (currently €12,679) used to determine total exemption from the property tax (taxe foncière) for a household with the reference number of 'parts' under the quotient familial. It is used in tpr_fr/ArithOp as the Formula parameter, whose function comment 'Calculate threshold for total exemption with quotient familial' shows it combines with $tpr_threshold2 (the per-additional-part increment) to build a household-specific income ceiling below which a taxpayer is fully exempt from property tax. This mirrors the real French rule exempting low-income, elderly or disabled households from taxe foncière based on income adjusted for family composition. The supplied 'taxes' theme note does not document this mechanism, so the reading relies on the constant's label, name, and the ArithOp function comment.
